chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever says, 'So-and-so is divorced if I marry her, and so-and-so is freed if I buy him,' then let him marry and let him buy, for divorce and manumission do not enter upon him (i.e., they do not take effect)."
ai.seo_question: Does conditional divorce take effect immediately or only after the condition is met?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the conditional divorce formula 'If I marry her, she is divorced' is analyzed to determine whether the condition is the marriage itself or the utterance. The Imam clarifies that since the condition is the act of marrying, the divorce does not take effect until the marriage is actually consummated or completed, preventing immediate legal consequences from the mere words. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the precise linkage between the conditional clause and the actualized act, distinguishing it from immediate divorce formulas.
